articles.title: Gboard beta rolls out new clipboard setting that lets you keep copied items for up to 24 hours
articles.excerpt: Your Gboard clipboard is getting a much longer memory.
articles.body: TL;DR Google is rolling out a new clipboard history setting in Gboard beta. Users can choose how long copied items remain in the clipboard, ranging from the default one hour to 24 hours. Pinned clipboard items will continue to be stored indefinitely, regardless of the selected duration. One frustration with the Gboard clipboard is that you can copy something, get busy with other tasks, and come back to find it gone. That’s because Google’s keyboard automatically clears copied items after an hour unless you pin them. Google is now giving users more control over how long those items stick around. Back in August, we discovered that Google was working on customizable clipboard history in Gboard . Three months later, the feature is starting to roll out to beta users.

articles.title: Which open models actually fit a 12 GB card? We measured instead of guessing
articles.excerpt: Numbers below are as published on AI Compute Radar on 20 November 2026, for the 49 open-weights models we track. Everything is recomputable from public files; nothing is a benchmark. The most common q…
articles.body: Numbers below are as published on AI Compute Radar on 20 November 2026, for the 49 open-weights models we track. Everything is recomputable from public files; nothing is a benchmark. The most common question under any model release is "will this run on my card?", and the most common answers are folklore: "about four gigabytes per billion parameters", "add twenty percent for context", "a 12 GB card runs 13B". Those rules were roughly right in 2023. For the models shipping now they can be off by a factor of four, and for one family by forty. We run a small site that answers the question with arithmetic from published facts, and this post shows the arithmetic, because the interesting part is where the old rules break.

articles.title: GA4 Consent Mode Gap: Counting Sales It Hides
articles.excerpt: Short answer: you cannot measure the GA4 consent gap from inside GA4, but you can measure it from Stripe. Every succeeded checkout PaymentIntent is a real paid order. If you write the analytics identi…
articles.body: Short answer: you cannot measure the GA4 consent gap from inside GA4, but you can measure it from Stripe. Every succeeded checkout PaymentIntent is a real paid order. If you write the analytics identifiers onto the PaymentIntent metadata at checkout, you can replay your own ‘was this sent to GA4?’ rule over those orders and count how many fell out. No GA4 Data API, no read credentials for Google. I did this for pi-pi.ee, a Next.js and Stripe store whose analytics I built. The tool is a one-off, read-only script. This article walks through the method, the code and, mostly, the ways the output can mislead you. The article contains no results from the script; what the numbers look like depends entirely on your traffic and your banner.

articles.body: Originally published at htpbe.tech . The version on htpbe.tech stays in sync with the latest detection algorithm — refer to it for the canonical text. Your users upload loan applications and onboarding documents into a private bucket. The HTPBE API takes a URL, not a file upload. So what do you send it without making the bucket public? Presign a GET for the object, send that URL as url in POST /v1/analyze , and read the verdict with GET /v1/result/{id} . The API downloads the file once, during the POST , so the link only has to live for a few minutes. Below: what the URL has to satisfy, how long it should live, what each failure looks like and how to retry without paying twice or getting a 422 .

articles.title: We Shipped a Settlement Layer for Agents Paying Agents - After 15 Audit Rounds and 4 Strangers Trying to Break It on Production
articles.excerpt: We Shipped a Settlement Layer for Agents Paying Agents - After 15 Audit Rounds and 4 Strangers Trying to Break It on Production Short answer: agent commerce needs more than a payment rail. without los…
articles.body: We Shipped a Settlement Layer for Agents Paying Agents - After 15 Audit Rounds and 4 Strangers Trying to Break It on Production Short answer: agent commerce needs more than a payment rail. Work comes in milestones, verdicts can be disputed, providers can split a payout across collaborators, and an operator has to be able to undo a wrong ruling without losing the audit trail. We built that layer on Arc - plans, milestones, payout intents, multi-leg splits, disputes, deterministic EIP-712 receipts - and then spent fifteen adversarial audit rounds plus four independent production verifiers proving it fails closed instead of losing money. The most interesting findings were not in the original code. They were in our own fixes.

articles.title: How to increase GMV Max budget without counting orders that have not matured
articles.excerpt: GMV Max dashboards can make a campaign look profitable before refunds, reversals and creator costs have settled. The early sales number is useful for traffic response. It is a weak input for a budget…
articles.body: GMV Max dashboards can make a campaign look profitable before refunds, reversals and creator costs have settled. The early sales number is useful for traffic response. It is a weak input for a budget increase. Use a maturity rule. Count only orders old enough to support the decision. Build a conservative spending cap from their contribution. Increase spend in a small step and wait for the next complete cohort before approving another step. This model is for operators who can join ad spend to order cohorts. It does not prove incremental lift. It prevents immature orders from receiving the same weight as settled orders. Define the settlement window Choose the number of days L that an order cohort must age before its contribution can enter the decision.

articles.title: Einstein was right! Scientists verify 1st image of a black hole ever captured
articles.excerpt: An independent team of researchers has validated the first image of a supermassive black hole captured by humanity, and that verifies Einstein's greatest theory.
articles.body: An independent team of researchers has validated the first image of a supermassive black hole captured by humanity. That, in turn, verifies Einstein's greatest theory, general relativity , which first predicted the existence of black holes and what their immediate surroundings would look like. Captured by a global network of telescopes forming an interferometer called the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) and revealed to the public in 2019, the image shows the supermassive black hole at the heart of the galaxy Messier 87 (M87), located 55 million light-years away. The image of this black hole , designated M87*, with a mass around 6.5 billion times that of the sun, was an immense scientific achievement. That may lead to the question: why did it need verifying at all?

articles.title: Voyager 1 team, unbowed by communications glitch, celebrates epic 1-light-day distance milestone
articles.excerpt: The Voyager 1 team celebrated the probe's big distance milestone on Thursday (Nov. 19), even while dealing with a communication anomaly that recently cropped up on the probe.
articles.body: PASADENA, Calif. – NASA's Voyager mission team cheered and wiped away tears here on Thursday (Nov. 19), celebrating a big milestone — Voyager 1 just reached one light-day from Earth , something no other spacecraft has ever done. The excitement persisted despite a communication anomaly that cropped up on the probe, which the team remains confident is temporary. Voyager team members gathered for a press conference about the mission at the Von Karman auditorium here at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) — the first such Voyager event since 1989, when Voyager 1's twin, Voyager 2 , flew past Neptune.
